Params: After the Success of the Second Styx Crossing
Day 31\nAfter the Success of the Second Styx Crossing\nLunch Break.
At Babylonia's Administrative Division, there is a corridor that is the narrowest, darkest, and most out-of-the-way in the building.
At the end of that corridor sits a small office with a blank nameplate.
A figure in a trench coat strides straight in, letting the shriek of the door hinge announce him.
I understand the reason, but I can't help feeling a little put out watching you sit here and brew tea every day.
The man behind the narrow desk already has a cup of tea waiting for him, alongside a box of fresh pastries beside it.
I am suspended and being investigated. I have no rank and no authority. Surely the President wouldn't complain about what few small pleasures I can legally enjoy, right?
Hassen sits down across the desk, taking a moment to find somewhere comfortable to put his legs.
I would, actually. This office is smaller than my storage closet, and there's nowhere to stretch my legs.
A small place has its perks. Nobody comes to hold meetings here.
Sure, you don't have to go to meetings... but you haven't exactly been resting either, from what I can tell.
Who was it that practically camped outside the Star of Life when the frontline troops came back, refusing to leave until every last injured human and Construct was out of the woods?
Wells taps the rim of his cup twice with his teaspoon.
The President of Babylonia raises an eyebrow and a hand, then lifts his teacup, indicating that he will drop the topic.
Let this busy man who goes to all the meetings fill you in on what's been going on out there.
None of that. I doubt you're short on ways to find out the classified stuff anyway.
That's a loaded accusation, especially given my current situation.
Hassen fixes Wells with a meaningful look from his one remaining eye for two whole seconds, and Wells finally sets down the teaspoon with a sigh.
The shattered "Understanding" Sefirah appears to be beyond repair, the wounded Arius was taken by the agent codenamed Aisling through unknown means, and all parties are currently in pursuit.

The World Government is working with the TEC's families to rebuild the Atlantic Eye, while also negotiating over ownership of that technology, its future applications, and revisions to the relevant legislation.
Before Project Atlas officially steps into the spotlight, the Science Council and the Watcher Society will continue their research.

They're exploring the Atlantic Eye for traces of Ananke and clearing out the residual Red Tide, with plans to establish a testing site for the <phonetic=A.O. Device>Atlas-Omega Device</phonetic> there.

The biggest recent discovery is that the Omega Weapon designed to absorb Red Tide has unexpectedly disabled Ananke's spacetime lock, while leaving its energy transmission intact. Asimov has been in total seclusion since.
Then there's the reparations and oversight that the Great Family Council eluded after the first Atlantic Calamity, the question of who owns the Balder, and a handful of other loose ends.
I'm done talking. Anything else you want to hear?
Mm, thorough as ever. I've nothing to add on my end.
But I doubt you've been asking around about what I have to tell you.
Hassen sits straight and rests his elbows on the desk.
Do you know who's been pushing the hardest to get you reinstated?
I'm flattered, but no. The only free time I have is this half hour at noon, here with you.
The man in the draped coat runs a finger along his stubble, his eyes narrowing slightly.
But what I did really pissed him off.
Don't take Nikola at face value. Sure, he can't stand your whole "strike-without-warning" act. But think about the workload that landed on him after you left. Trust me... he missed you terribly.
...But no, it's not him either. Guess again. Think of the last person you'd expect.
A look of genuine confusion crosses Wells' face, his brow slowly knitting together. Then, one eyebrow shoots up.
Hassen nods, struggling to keep a straight face.
The battle-hardened former Chief of Staff stares back with a blank expression.
Think about it. If you don't come back, all those under-the-table deals the two of you had going would be dead in the water.
And you're the one heading up Project Atlas. You really think he'd let a seat at that table slip through his fingers?
So there he is, cursing under his breath while showing up at the Control Court every other day to grease the wheels for you.
The two middle-aged men shake with laughter in the cramped little office, only stopping after a good while.
Hassen leans back in his chair, his eyes drifting to the rare sliver of sunlight filtering in through the window.
All's well that ends well, but it was a knife's edge the whole way through. You haven't made a gamble like that in years.
Stepping into the spotlight to draw out the vipers lurking in Babylonia... You'll be sleeping with one eye open from here on out.
Sometimes the best way to get what you want is to throw them off the rhythm and make a move they never saw coming.
After calculating probability and using logic for over a decade, you went and bet on the goodness in people. Still holding onto that, are you?
The chestnut-haired man cradles his teacup and blows away the steam with warmth and a hint of mischief in his smile, the same as when he was young.
There is a small silver falcon pin on his lapel now.
Isn't that what got us here after all this time? Holding onto what we believed in and having the courage to fight for it?
Well said. I'm stealing that for my end-of-year speech.
When have you ever written your own end-of-year speech?
Hassen elects not to hear that, and reaches across Wells for the box of pastries.
The pastries from that maple lemon waffle place Allen recommended always smell so tempting.
Those are not for you. Celica mentioned you're cutting back on sugar.
That's a problem, then. Someone else is on his way, and there's definitely not enough for you to share.
Another one? There's no room to—
The words are barely out of his mouth when the door swings open again.
Babylonia's military commander stands in the doorway, sees the waffle box, and furrows his brow at his former subordinate.
Your reinstatement papers just hit your desk. Sign them and be done with it. There's a meeting this afternoon.
He then turns to Hassen, who has quietly helped himself to a piece of waffle.
And you—now I know where you've been sneaking off to every lunch break. Get back to work!
Can you really bring yourself to walk away from these pastries while they're still warm?
Seeing as we'll have plenty of time to savor our work later, I move that we take a moment to savor our snacks.
He passes a fork to Nikola.
The white-haired commander pauses for just a beat, then slips inside and pulls the door shut behind him.
The creaky old door, for once, is finally left in peace.
Above the Dam of the Atlantic Eye
Later That Day\nAbove the Dam of the Atlantic Eye
Once abandoned and twice destroyed, the dam's docking port is bustling with people once more under the clear skies.
From the moment you step off the aircraft, the two of you are met with a steady stream of warm greetings from faces you do not quite recognize but who seem genuinely glad to see you.
Their uniforms are a mismatched assortment. Looking closer, you find there is something amusing about trying to place them all, because this is not a sight anyone would have expected to see—
Port Podesta dockworkers are huddling over blueprints with Engineering Force Constructs. You can hear the Constructs asking the workers how to build a surfboard as cool as their captain's.

Sailors from the Balder gesture animatedly at an airship alongside engineers from the Watcher Society, while someone from the Cosmos Technicians Union stands nearby, apparently trying to keep the peace.
Weaving through the crowd, the pink-haired engineer arrives in front of the two of you, and the first thing he does is circle Adelyde three times with his arms folded.
Not bad, not a scratch on you! You Constructs recover so fast!

—What this old friend of Adelyde's neglects to mention is that he nearly flooded the chamber with the repair pod with his tears a month ago when he saw her lying there, gravely wounded and unconscious.
Neither of you has told him about your close call with the Sefirah yet.
Adelyde shakes her head with a resigned sigh, though the smile tugging at the corner of her mouth gives away how she is feeling.
Don't you worry about a thing.
Isn't it almost time for the Atlas Tower's trial launch? Why aren't you rushing us over there already?
Who said I wasn't?! I've been waiting on you two! Come on, let's go!
As Aristo leads you through the crowd, the sea of people begins flowing in the same direction.

We swapped out the beacon tower's internal power supply for the one powering the Omega Device. The structure's a bit different from the launchers on the Balder, so the output wasn't great at first, but we figured it out—

Your brain quietly filters out the incomprehensible jargon, and the curly-haired engineer, lost in the joy of his own explanation, slowly transforms into a sea otter cracking open a shell in your eyes.
You steal a glance at Adelyde, and you can tell she feels the same.
The two of you exchange a look and stifle your laughter, turning away just enough so Aristo cannot see.
Reaching the boundary of the viewing area, the three of you turn to wave at the cheering crowd before continuing toward the base of the tower.
Aristo hands Adelyde and you a headset each.
What was once Atlantic Eye's Day of Enlightenment will now live on as the launch date of the Atlas Tower. For so many people, getting to celebrate it together again means everything.
This is the best spot to watch from. I have to head inside to man the control panel, so I'll miss the most spectacular moment, but I'm still going to make a wish with you guys.
Take one each. Count down the last ten seconds of the hour, and we'll light it when it hits zero.
From the headset, you can hear the researchers of Project Atlas frantically run their final checks. Outside the headset, voices swell like a tide in the distance.
A sudden calmness settles over you.
Maybe the most satisfying moment in the world is the one just before something wonderful happens.
You seem a lot more relaxed than you used to be.
Maybe it's because I finally don't have to keep secrets about that mysterious sailor and the looming crisis anymore.
I couldn't imagine where I'd go and what I'd do once that crisis had passed.
It was like the star I used to navigate by had fallen onto my ship. A wonderful surprise... but then where was I supposed to sail?
But now that I'm here, I realize I never needed to worry about it at all.
—Because the moment I stepped out of the repair pod, next semester's F.O.S. teaching schedule was already waiting in my terminal.
It's not easy to be a student or a teacher...
Thank you for your hard work...
As the moment draws near, the crowd stirs with anticipation.
You traveled to the past so many times, and not once did we get to celebrate the Day of Enlightenment together.
Maybe we've been waiting for today.
The best things are always worth the wait.
We're in charge of the countdown, so we'll have to make our wishes a little early.
I wish to adopt a Bourbon rose from the Babylonia greenhouse and keep it alive.
I want to make a hamburger steak sandwich myself one day, even if I can barely remember what it's supposed to taste like.
I want to properly introduce you to the people you only met in Ananke.
Why do I still feel like I'm talking to a phantom who agrees with everything?
It's good that there are things you want in your life.
If you remember these little things, your mind is unharmed. Well done, me!
(Make a finger gun and tap Adelyde on her arm)
There are plenty more I want, but there's no rush. I'll share them with you in the future.
Would you like an epic ode instead? I did receive a classical education, you know.
Heh, I'll show my gratitude in my own way. Just you wait.
Adelyde lets out a laugh, then mirrors the gesture of your past promises and taps back.
Her eyes hold a hearth-like warmth.
A brilliant beam of light surges from the tower's peak, piercing the sky and blossoming into a shield at its apex.
The golden light swirls like a dancing sun, and the blue light breathes like an open sky.
All readings stable! Punishing Virus concentration at zero—
This Clean Zone trial run is a success!
From this day forward, the Atlantic Eye will no longer be a vestige of calamity, a monolith for families to fight over, or a proving ground for personal ambition.
It will be a beacon of hope, a fortress that belongs to all of humanity.
Her braids are lifted in the wind, her red coat snapping around her.
And there's one more wish I can make come true right now.
Adelyde stops at the edge of the docking port, a hundred meters above ground, and glances back with a wink.
She steps out into the open air, and vanishes in an instant.
A second later, a sleek crimson airship launches upward with her aboard, cutting through the air like a swordfish breaking the surface and hovering right in front of you.
Adelyde extends her hand toward you.
No matter what name you go by, or what role you play... come with me, into the future.
Every soul, every era has its own odyssey, where we meet and part with each other across the endless voyage.
But these meetings and partings are not without meaning.
Because our conviction has the power to cross time and space, and this faith can bind fractured worlds and people back together.
Kindred spirits always find each other along the way, and in doing so, produce the brightest moments of one another's lives.
We do not walk alone, and we will never give up.
Into the storm we fly, bound for the blue beyond.
